incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PD-8342 fired — metric: cuda_mmap_failure_rate in eu-west-1 crossed threshold (pool=rwd-eu-gpu-pool-7). auto-escalation=60s.

pagerduty-bot: Incident URL: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-8342 — severity: high. Affected service: inference-gpu-serving.

Maya (oncall): I'm on call. Acking PD now. Will grab logs and check node state.

Maya (oncall): quick status: customer-facing error symptoms = increased 5xx from hosted API on eu-west region, sporadic failed allocations, some requests falling back to smaller model.

Sam (sre): Can you paste the last few container logs for a failing task? Also want nvidia-smi and dmesg grep.

Maya (oncall): paste: ```
[2026-07-12T10:03:12Z] inference-pod-72ffd: runtime error: mmap failed: Cannot allocate memory (errno=12)
[2026-07-12T10:03:12Z] inference-pod-72ffd: CUDA error: failed to map memory region (0x7f8a2c000000)
[2026-07-12T10:03:13Z] inference-pod-72ffd: falling back to model-quantized-v2
```

Maya (oncall): nvidia-smi output (node gpu-45): ```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.54.03    Driver Version: 535.54.03    CUDA Version: 12.2     |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
|  0  A100-SXM4...     Off        00000000:65:00.0 Off |                    0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Maya (oncall): dmesg shows repeated: ```
[ 1234.567890] mmap: failed to allocate gpu pinned memory: -12
[ 1234.568001] cuda: vma_alloc failed for 0x7f8a2c000000 size=16777216
```

Leila (infra): ok that's consistent with a kernel-level mmap failure on that node class. Could be fragmentation + pinned memory pressure. Any recent deployments or config changes?

Arthur (ml-runtime): We had a subtle regression in KV cache prefetch last rollout earlier today that increases pinned memory briefly for large batch requests. It was deployed to eu-west canary at 09:30. Rolling back that canary would be my first try.

Maya (oncall): Noted. Rolling back rollout for kv-prefetch feature flag on eu-west now. Command: `redwoodctl rollout cancel kv-prefetch --env=eu-west --force`

Maya (oncall): done — canary toggled off. Observability: mmap failures rate dropped ~40% in the last 30s.

Sam (sre): Good. Immediate mitigation: 1) keep kv-prefetch off; 2) add two spare instances to pool to spread allocation spikes; 3) reroute heavy customers to fallback pool where memory compaction is disabled.

Maya (oncall): scaling pool now: `redwoodctl pool scale rwd-eu-gpu-pool-7 --add 2 --reason "mitigate mmap spikes PD-8342"`

Maya (oncall): scale command accepted, new instances requested — ETA ~90s.

pagerduty-bot: PD-8342 updated: acknowledged by Maya. Escalation canceled.

CS - Sheridan: Which customers were impacted? Need to notify SRE + CS for affected tenants.

Maya (oncall): Initial query shows two customers with elevated errors: acme-corp and beta-saas — both on dedicated routing in eu-west and heavy batching. Error counts: acme-corp 5xx spike 12% -> baseline 0.2%; beta-saas 5xx spike 8%.

Leila (infra): I'll open a customer-impact ticket and ping CS to prepare messaging. If rollback + scale holds, impact should be transient.

Arthur (ml-runtime): Follow-up: we should change the allocator flags for the runtime to reduce pinned allocations per-request as a medium-term fix. I'll open a PR after initial containment.

Maya (oncall): After scale, mmap failures dropped another ~50%. Still seeing occasional hits on node gpu-45. I'm going to cordon gpu-45 to stop scheduling new pods while we drain problematic pods. Doing: `kubectl cordon gpu-45 && kubectl drain gpu-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

Sam (sre): Be careful with drain; we don't want to cause global capacity issues. Confirm you have adequate spare capacity (we just added 2).

Maya (oncall): Confirmed. Drain started. Affected pods restarted onto new nodes and passed healthchecks.

pagerduty-bot: PD-8342 note: L2 oncall (Sam) joined the incident channel per escalation policy.

Sam (sre): I'll help monitor logs and follow up on kernel reports. Can you collect `sudo cat /proc/meminfo` and `sudo pmap` for the node before it reboots? We want to see fragmentation patterns.

Maya (oncall): Collected /proc/meminfo snapshot attached in the incident ticket.

Maya (oncall): brief customer impact summary for CS: two customers saw elevated 5xx and increased tail latency for ~9 minutes, automatic fallbacks allowed some traffic to succeed, no data loss reported.

CS - Sheridan: Ok will draft a short message: "Transient errors in eu-west affecting inference requests for a subset of customers; mitigation applied; follow-up with root cause once investigation complete."

Arthur (ml-runtime): Note for follow-up runbook actions: 1) revert aggressive KV prefetch defaults; 2) add automatic temporary routing to fallback pool on mmap errors; 3) add a node-level memory defragmentation check to autoscaler.

Leila (infra): Adding post-incident action item: add gpu-45 to hardware investigation (possible driver/kernel interaction) and schedule a maintenance window if we see recurrence.

Maya (oncall): PD-8342 status -> mitigated. I'll leave the thread open for 1h to watch and then declare resolved if stable.

Sam (sre): +1. Create an incidents postmortem and assign to Arthur + Leila.

Maya (oncall): created incident doc in /incidents/PD-8342 and added initial timeline + logs. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/PD-8342

Maya (oncall): final note: if anyone sees a repeat spike, escalate to pagerduty PD-8342 and tag this thread. :thumbsup:
